title: Same Ba ang Export at Import Electricity Rate?
audience: Net-metering customers and buyers sizing for export
premise: Imports are billed at the full retail rate; export credit is based on the blended generation cost, so each exported kWh is worth less than an imported one.
scriptBasis: Claude draft from the episode plan (data/episodes.json) title/angle, V1.1 brand lines; claims checked online 2026-11-25.

sources: Sources: Meralco Solar & Net Metering (FAQ 11); Meralco schedule of
rates (Nov 2026); DOE REMB Net Metering (checked 25 Nov 2026)

cues.text: Pareho ba ang presyo ng kuryenteng binibili at ine-export mo?
Ang binibili mo sa grid, buong retail rate ang singil.
Ang ine-export mo, blended generation cost ang basehan ng credit.
Kaya mas mababa ang credit kada kWh kaysa sa binabayaran mo.
cues.say: Kaya mas mababa ang credit kada kilowatt-hour kaysa sa binabayaran mo.

cues.text: Kaya mas sulit gamitin ang solar habang may araw.
Tamang laki ng system ang susi, hindi puro export.
Dahil ang gusto ni Kuya SoLight… naka-solar ka na, SoSmart ka pa!

sources.title: Net Metering Program presentation
excerpts: Qualified end-users apply with their distribution utility; net-metering uses metering that records both import and export energy.
Interim pricing for export energy is the DU's monthly blended generation cost.

sources.title: Solar and Net Metering
excerpts: Your system supplies the property first while it is generating.
The Meralco grid supplies the property when renewable generation is not enough.
an exported kilowatt-hour is not exchanged one-for-one at the full retail rate.
The Net Metering peso credit is applied to eligible bill charges under the current rules,
based on the applicable monthly blended generation cost rather than the full retail rate. (FAQ 11)
